Technical details +

Growth on a supplied tissue outline. Both views come from the same model state. Your click only adds electrical current. It never paints the tissue directly; whatever changes comes from what the model learned. The model is never shown the finished tissue. What this model can and cannot do yet is listed in Evidence and limits.

The electrical map and the visible tissue are two descriptions of one system. The rule stays fixed as the state evolves. A local input changes the model's electrical conditions; the learned dynamics determine what follows.

Voltage here is a unitless stand-in, not a real measurement. Scientists call more negative regions hyperpolarized and more positive regions depolarized. These colors are not calibrated membrane-potential readings.

A shared rule.
A collective pattern.

It's a neural cellular automaton, meaning every cell runs the same small neural network that only sees its neighbors.

Technical details

Each cell reads its own state, signals from its neighbors, and a limited memory of those connections. Repeat that step many times and the larger tissue pattern appears.

On top of that, each connection between neighbors keeps a fast memory and a slow memory, and the fast one gradually settles into the slow one. That idea is borrowed from the Dragon Hatchling (BDH) AI model. Ours is a small mix of the two ideas, not a copy of the Dragon Hatchling language model.

What is learned, and what is supplied. During training, the model is shown made-up examples of normal tissue: its shape and its electrical and chemical patterns. When it runs, we give the model a rough outline of the tissue to start from (the "precursor"), plus faint signals and a front-to-back direction. The head, tail and eye regions are not in that starting outline; anything that appears is grown by the model. We set the speeds, which cells connect, and the memory rules by hand. What the network learns is the growth step itself.

How the browser runs the Python model. Everything runs in your browser, with no server. This page loads the original trained weights (the model's learned numbers, stored as float32) and runs our own JavaScript copy of the model's update step in the background. The copy keeps every value each cell holds, both connection memories, delayed long-range messages, empty edges at the border, and updates all cells from the same snapshot. Before release it is checked against the original Python model.

Make the result
inspectable.

A useful experiment makes its assumptions visible. These are the capabilities and limits recorded for the supplied checkpoint.

↗

Normal pattern formation

Learned face-like electrical fields and normal planarian identity fields on synthetic tissue scaffolds.

DEMONSTRATED
○

Alternative anatomy

Persistent two-headed planaria and ectopic eyes were not demonstrated by the tested electrical interventions.

OPEN EXPERIMENT
○

Regeneration

The delivered damage test retained a visible tissue gap. Anatomical regeneration is not established.

OPEN EXPERIMENT

The data are procedural, dimensionless proxies. Grid sites represent tissue patches. These results do not establish biological predictive accuracy or drug-response validity.
